new_packages.label: תִּיקּוּן וְנוּן פְּשׁוּטָה — הַשְׁלֵמוּת הָרְאוּיָה
new_packages.label_en: Tikkun and the Straight Nun — Wholeness Restored
new_packages.reason: The Torah explicitly identifies the aspired-to state as תִּיקּוּן (complete repair), and the structural token of that state is the נוּן פְּשׁוּטָה (straight/final nun) standing upright in its place. These two concepts share the same essential nature: the presence of the straight nun IS tikkun; tikkun IS the state where the nun stands straight and complete. This is not cause-and-effect — the upright nun does not produce tikkun, it IS tikkun made visible in letterform. The closing prayer of the Torah ('may the kinot be transformed into tikkun, and may the teiku be repaired') declares this as the redemptive goal. This good package is the direct mirror of Package 1 (the exile/deficiency package).

source_evidence.quote: וְיִתְהַפְּכוּ הַקִּינוֹת לְתִּיקּוּן, וְיִתְתַּקֵּן הַתֵּיקוּ הַנַּ"ל
source_evidence.note: The closing prayer establishes tikkun as the positive redemptive pole, the counterpart of teiku and kinot.

source_evidence.quote: שֶׁנֶּחְסָר הַנּוּן שֶׁל תִּיקּוּן וְנַעֲשֶׂה תֵּיקוּ
source_evidence.note: Tikkun is defined by the presence of its nun — the nun IS the completion of tikkun, making them bechina-equivalent.

new_packages.threshold_check: The new package requirement is 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. Torah #247 is only 2 sentences and is extremely compact. Tikkun and the straight nun are connected by direct implication from the text's core mechanism (the removal of the nun = the removal of tikkun = the creation of teiku). While the text does not use the word 'בְּחִינַת' explicitly for the pair tikkun/nun-peshutat, the entire argument rests on their identity. This proposed package has only 2 nodes, which is below the strict threshold of 3. RECOMMENDATION: This package is strongly implied but technically marginal on the 3-concept threshold. It is proposed because the good/evil mirror structure demands it — without the tikkun package, the teaching's binary structure (exile vs. redemption, bent nun vs. straight nun) is only half-represented in the dataset. The reviewer should decide whether to accept this 2-node good-mirror package or hold it pending additional data entry that may bring in more tikkun-related concepts for this Torah.
